steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: We're almost at our destination.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: What? You'd never would've reached the Stultifera in one piece without me. The children of the sea would've ripped you apart, crushed you, or bound your limbs as they dragged you off to their nests.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You're not like Quintus.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: What might could you be talking about? My skin? This sack of flesh?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: None of that matters.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: What are you trying to accomplish?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: And what are YOU trying to accomplish, Hunter? Your kind already loathe your enemies while simultaneously doubting the purity of your own blood. But still... you pretend to be calm.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: What are you trying to get out of me?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Silence. A wise choice. Ægir are not a sociable lot, it is known. But it seems there are exceptions.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Or, are you just a bit of an unpopular grump?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: I can answer your question. Quintus wouldn't, nor will other humans. But the Seaborn will. Like Heralds, we come to understand things. We are not limited by the way humans think.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I don't need your riddles.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Before coming here, I was in the midst of translating a literary classic from Ursus. It was about race and nations. About history. I was putting it into Iberian and Victorian.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Take a look, Mister Hunter.
Ulpianus's gaze follows the woman's hand, his eyes subconsciously drawn towards the ocean.
A pitch-black sea. Dense with dark clouds. Oppressive. And yet, a vague outline of the starry sky is visible.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Even the Ægir rarely look out across the ocean from the water's surface. Different races, different countries. The land is fractured in every sense, and its conflicts are neverending.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: But when you look over the boundless sea, do you see anything representing those divides?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Tch... These damn monsters!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Jordi! Are you alright?!

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Slithering sounds, rubbing against the wall)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: G-Get away from me—!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Seems like activating this facility has made these poor creatures realize that this place doesn't make a very good nest.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: High Inquisitor!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Keep ascending, Ægir. Your hands are for wielding tools, not fire and steel.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: The plan is unchanged. Go with Irene and find what the Inquisition and the Hunters are seeking.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I, I know! Please be careful!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Do you really think we can find that ship?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It can only pass through Iberia.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't understand... If it is a place like Rhodes Island, why hasn't it tried to return in sixty years?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We too are lost, unable to find a way back home. Is that not so?

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Sounds of stirring, slapping the water)

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The children are increasing in number.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...Are you alright?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Me? Why do you ask?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You didn't speak a single word on the way to Iberia.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Have you always seen me as a chatterbox, Skadi?
Skadi stares deeply into Specter's eyes.
When she'd finally found Laurentina on land, her eyes were clouded over.
Then she saw it in Sal Viento. A fragment of Laurentina as she was. But it was short-lived. After returning to Rhodes Island, she seemed to have fallen back into the abyss.
But now, Skadi begins to find herself unable to distinguish which corner of Specter's mind she is currently dealing with.
She has an ominous guess.
One that has always swirled through her mind.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No need to overthink this, Skadi.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And the same goes for you, my sleepy little mermaid. We don't have much time. You will awaken.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Will I?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You will.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: For the time being... Go with Shark and take out the small fry. Their numbers are endless, so remember to adjust your breathing and conserve energy.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You should already know that I prefer it that way.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...Must we be in such a hurry to perform again? The storm is not yet ready.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Heh, but it seems our dance partner won't be kept waiting.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Tch, there's no end to them.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Doña Irene!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: You're still alive! So that flash of light was from the High Inquisitor's lantern after all!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um, he wanted us to continue on... But what exactly should we do? Keep searching for the ship's location?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I was originally planning to wait for the technicians to arrive, but seeing how you got this big fella started all by yourself—

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: Hiss... Hiss...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —Make every second count!

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: Thiago? So you're finally seeing clearly.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Why haven't you fled? The Penal Battalion and that Inquisitor have been lying in ambush in town.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: Then why haven't your proud townspeople returned?

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: The Inquisitors have already taken away all the confused, directionless residents of Gran Faro, and you already know what's going to happen to them.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: You know all too well.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: But I can't sit by and watch Gran Faro go up in smoke. I have to do whatever I can.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: You? Fight the Inquisition? Fair enough, Thiago. But that will only hasten the town's demise. Iberia will never tolerate an act of treason.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: While we welcome all into our fold, but the weak do not have that right. This 'determination' of yours is but a sick joke your mind is playing on you. You understand nothing. Who do you think you're talking to?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Who? If I'd cared enough to investigate, you would've been flushed out by the Penal Battalion long ago.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Tell me then, what can people like you offer Gran Faro?

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: In the end, this town is... a mere human settlement.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: What we seek to offer up to this land is of a much higher calling than your meaningless baubles.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (A slithering sound emerges from cracks in the building)

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: You've been followed.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: Hiss...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hah, these Sea Terrors have pretty sharp senses.

steps.name: Bizarre Cultist
steps.text: An outsider? We will allow it. Your flesh and blood shall become nourishment for our wounded. We all give back to this land.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Tch, the nethersea brand has already reached this far. The walls, the stairs, it's all over the place!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Are you still not done yet? They're getting closer!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Almost there!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: How does this make any sense? Even after all these years, the signal-receiving devices are still operable... But why? How?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Oh, the logs—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: —Woah, there it is! Now let's take a look—

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: Hiss...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Ugh—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (Their numbers are exploding! They're moving through the nethersea brand, as if they've merged with the ground entirely!)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (At this rate, even Maestro and the Hunters won't be able to stay in this branded place for much longer...)

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Rough sounds of slithering across the floor)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Damn it— Underneath us! Jordi!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wh-What?!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Continue.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah, um... Okay...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Abyssal Hunters!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You're too weak. Swarms like this require swifter movements. Spare yourself the energy to breathe.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Like so.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Urgh...!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How much longer, Ægir?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Th-There are no records in the logs of how to operate these information terminals, so I'll have to keep searching—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: —There's some data here... I don't understand what it means, but it keeps popping up!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Keeps popping up? Even if that's from the Inquisition's last attempt, that should've been years ago!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I, I'm not sure. I assumed the data loss was caused by a power outage, b-but—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: If my hypothesis is right...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: There's a ship that's been sending signals to this lighthouse for decades!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How far away it is?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I know, I'm looking... Ugh, where are the navigation records—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...It's very close.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: How can it be... so close?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Waaaah!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Wh-What happened?!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I'm afraid the underground portion of the tower has been swallowed up by the nethersea brand.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: We need to make our decision, now!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Decision? What decision? If we have the means to locate the ship, then we will go.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: No! We should eradicate the Sea Terrors to ensure that the Penal Battalion's reinforcements can arrive safely!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Impossible. You will merely wear yourselves out before the stronger prey can even join the hunt.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Or do you mean to say that Iberia has hundreds upon thousands of people willing to hold the line to their dying breath, like the High Inquisitor below us?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: No, but—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Opportunity waits for no one.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Have you confirmed the coordinates?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah, um, I can determine an approximate range, but I don't know why it's spinning around, or if that means—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It is being kept afloat by aberrant ocean currents. See that square surrounded by Seaborn? That's what the ship looks like now.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But, that ship is the only vessel we have.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You can have it. We don't need it.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: No.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Go with them.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: High Inquisitor?! What did you just say?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: The Eye of Iberia has already been activated. There should still be some working safeguards in place.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Lord Carmen will arrive to purge the evil remaining along these shores. We don't have time to waste on these endless hordes.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Th-Then, I'll stay with you, sir!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: No. You ought to accompany them.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You should go see the ocean.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: What saved your life, what let the rescuers find you... wasn't me. It was the Scriptures you hold in your hand.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Make the right choice. Do not bring shame to Iberia.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Understood, High Inquisitor.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I will become Iberia's eyes, and return the Stultifera to our country's embrace.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Then go.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: I look forward to seeing the moment you pass down the correct verdict.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Yes, High Inquisitor!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You should leave too. Go with them.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Sir... I don't want to. I want to stay here.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: It's too dangerous.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I don't know a single thing about that golden vessel. The best I could do is bask in its magnificence, but... I don't think that's where my duty lies.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I, um, this might be a strange thing to say, but I... I only felt my own worth when I was exploring this lighthouse, so—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Please, let me stay here.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Exactly one hundred down. But nothing has changed.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: They're like stars in the sky.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Breaking the encirclement would be simple, but defending the lighthouse? How long would we be slashing away?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: What a fine, colorful carpet they make as their carcasses dissolve.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: A carpet of life... Ah, this must be the most beautiful carpet in the land.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (True, the nethersea brand is spreading, which means...)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Your weapons cannot burn them, but mine can.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: That's only a temporary solution. Cauterizing the tips of the seagrass won't stop it from growing.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: It's good enough. Grab your people and get out of here. Steer the ship out, or you won't be able to get your bearings.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You realize what that means.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You don't need to tell me, Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Very well. Do your best to survive, High Inquisitor.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark, Skadi!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That's the ship...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: After so long spent waiting on land, we are finally about to return to Ægir. We...
Gladiia's words slow to a halt.
Her hand caresses her neck. On her well-concealed skin is a patch that is rough to the touch.
The ship is right in front of her eyes. —No, don't be hasty, Gladiia. The ocean is still dangerous. Otherwise, it would not have trapped the three Hunters ashore.
But without a doubt, her heart is smoldering.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: They've left.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: That's right. Which means we're stranded here until the Penal Battalion's reinforcements arrive.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You've done well, Ægir, so you've earned the right to answer a question.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah, o-okay! I swear to answer truthfully!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Did you make your own decision to leave the shore, and come here with us?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You're just an ordinary person. Janitor or whatever, you are no warrior. Few can wander out to sea, let alone witness a battle against the Sea Terrors.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Yet... Look, your expression doesn't shake at all under the light of my lantern. What are you thinking? What do you want?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I can't even remember ever seeing my mother or father. Everyone always told me I'm an Ægir, and that we came here to repair the lighthouse. But it's all ruined.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... Before all this, I didn't know a single thing. I was lost and confused. To be honest, when the Sea Terrors came, Thi— Someone told me to leave as soon as possible. But...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Truthfully, I didn't even know where I could go.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Because I'm an Ægir, all I can do is keep my head down as I trudge through life. And, um... just so you know, I'm actually a chapel nurse, not a janitor.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But that doesn't really count as work, does it? All the things Mr. Elysium talks about, the way he acts... Maybe that's what it really means to live life upon this land.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: That's why... I felt like this was an opportunity.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Are you not afraid of death?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I don't think there's anyone who isn't, sir.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: I should be frank with you. The nethersea brand has already completely engulfed the coastline. We don't have much time left.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Lord Carmen and Dr. Kal'tsit may have their methods, but I'm not so optimistic.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: When the others left, we were basically condemned to death.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Is... that why you insisted on me going with them?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: It's too late to regret it now. You chose to defy me, of your own free will. But even if you die here, your death would be by no means meaningless.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You're not shaken.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Haha... Just a little bit, maybe. But even if I went with them, wouldn't I still have nine-to-one odds of dying?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: As long as I stay here in this lighthouse, I can at least feel like I've already—

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Don't be in such a hurry to give up.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: The Eye of Iberia should have its own defenses. Go start them up.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah, alright. But, where will you go?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Now...

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: We are alone at sea, far from our homeland.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Again and again we arrive on this little reef, the weight of our lives and of our vessels so much heavier than the place itself.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: ...Hiss...

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Swarms of slithering sounds)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Between the ocean and Iberia, there is no such thing as justice... or evil.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Only sword and lantern—

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Only me.
